text:
maria: quick heads-up — spotted a perf regression on long-seq traffic after yesterday's kernel-selector autotune push. tail p99 up ~30% for seq > 1024 :thinking:
jamal: Oof. Do we have a repro load? Was it the arch-aware pick or the seqlen-bin mapping change?
sophia: repro on staging with the streaming chat test harness. putting 2k requests with variable seqlen distribution (50% <128, 30% 128-1024, 20% >1024).
alex: I captured flamegraphs — looks like KV cache miss + path swap overhead. When kernel path switches mid-request we do an extra KV lookup and async driver handshake.
casey: Can you paste the logs? curious about key namespace and driver version tags.
maria: snippet from staging logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-14T14:00:12Z] driver=v2 kernel=fp16-archX seq_bin=>1024 key=rctx:driver_v1:modelA:bin3:prefix_9a ttl=300 hit=false
[2026-02-14T14:00:12Z] driver=v2 kernel=fp16-archX seq_bin=>1024 migrating_key=rctx:driver_v2:modelA:bin3:prefix_9a migrate=false
[2026-02-14T14:00:12Z] kernel-switch overhead=12ms kv_lookup=4ms
[2026-02-14T14:00:13Z] request id=... tail_latency=220ms
```
jamal: Ah — driver_version mismatch in key prefix. driver rolled to v2 but cache keys still using v1 names, so we do extra migration probes. That explains the miss storm.
sophia: Right — load causes frequent kernel-path choices, and when seqlen bin flips between nearby values we hit different salted keys. Lots of near-duplicate prefixes.
alex: Measured impact: with 10% traffic routed to v2 we saw 18% higher amortized token-ms and cache throughput drop due to churn.
casey: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) add a compatibility read that checks both v1 and v2 keys (bounded to 1 extra lookup) 2) warm up v2 keys proactively when rolling drivers 3) Minor: increase small TTL on newly written keys to avoid immediate eviction.
maria: agreed. long-term design: canonical key versioning + ephemeral session salt. idea: keep model-level namespace version that only increments on schema changes, not driver minor bumps. That reduces accidental namespace fragmentation.
jamal: +1. Also suggest a background migration process that writes v2 keys when v1 hits occur during a read, but we must rate-limit to avoid write storms.
sophia: Notes from the perf experiment:
- baseline p99 (seq>1024) = 170ms
- after autotune change (no mitigation) p99 = 220ms
- with compat-read (single extra lookup) p99 = 180ms, throughput -2%
- with proactive warmup p99 = 175ms, throughput unchanged
These are from 10k request batches.
alex: Concern: compat-read trades read amplification for latency. For high-traffic hot keys it might be fine, but for bursty loads it kills throughput. Maybe only enable compat-read when driver_version != namespace_version.
casey: Also saw weird behavior under GC pressure: when driver restarts we observed stale KV tombstones interpreted as hits -> kernel picked wrong path briefly. Need a deterministic invalidation signal from driver on clean shutdown.
infra-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout to production paused at 10% due to latency alerts (rule: p99_seq>1024 > 200ms).
maria: Action items:
- Jamal + Alex: implement compat-read gated by namespace_version check (10% canary) — due EOD
- Sophia: run extended soak with mix of seqlen distributions (48h) and collect token-ms and write amplification metrics — due 48h
- Casey: design driver shutdown invalidation handshake (proto sketch in thread) — due 3 days
- Ops: hold canary until mitigations land :thumbsup:
jamal: I'll open the PR and include microbenchmarks. Will also add rate-limit for background migration writes.
alex: I'll add a metric for "compat_lookups_per_k" and alert if > 500 per second.
sophia: I'll attach the test harness config in a follow-up thread (it has the exact request distributions).
maria: thanks team. keeping this thread open for rollout notes. :rocket:
